# Ayush Suryawanshi

> Ayush Suryawanshi is an Indian chemical engineer working across electrocatalyst synthesis, electrode preparation, electrochemical testing and process engineering. Ayush holds an M.Tech in Catalysis Technology from IIT Madras (2026, CGPA 8.51/10), spent a research semester at NTNU, Norway (2025), and is currently a Management Trainee at LOXIM Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad, working on effluent treatment technology. The work spans catalyst synthesis, electrode preparation and three-electrode electrochemical testing, DFT and reaction-kinetics modelling, and process design. Research interests include electrochemical energy conversion such as AEM electrolysis, fuel cells and green hydrogen.

## Education
- M.Tech, Catalysis Technology, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Madras, Chennai, Jun 2024 – May 2026. CGPA 8.51/10. Degree conferred at the 63rd convocation, 17 July 2026.
- Semester exchange, Department of Chemical Engineering, NTNU, Trondheim, Norway, Aug – Dec 2025. UTFORSK mobility scholarship. Thesis catalyst synthesis in the KinCat group, hosted and supervised by Prof. Edd Anders Blekkan.

## Experience
- Management Trainee, LOXIM Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad (Jul 2026 – present): Leading technology selection for sulphate removal from plant effluent. Options shortlisted so far point to a projected 50–60% lower operating cost, from INR 2.5/L to about INR 1.0–1.2/L. Evaluated electrocoagulation and electroflocculation as pretreatment options. Running screening, sample trials and feasibility checks with more than ten technology vendors. Trained on HPLC, GC-MS, FTIR and UV-Vis; completed plant safety induction and HSE training.
- Deputy Placement and Internship Coordinator, Placement and Internship Cell, IIT Madras (Aug 2024 – Jul 2025): Handled placements and internships for the 2023–25 and 2024–26 M.Tech batches; 75% of M.Tech chemical engineers were placed.

## Projects
- Keeping platinum clean in formic acid fuel cells (May 2025 – May 2026, IIT Madras, with synthesis at NTNU, Norway): Problem: Platinum oxidises formic acid well at first, but adsorbed CO builds up and the current falls within an hour. What I did: Made four Bi-modified Pt/C catalysts, tuned the catalyst ink, and tested them with and without a quinone mediator (AQSA). Key result: Bi(1.25)-Pt/C, with the least bismuth, kept 92.9% of its current over a one-hour hold, against 58.5% for commercial Pt/C. Limits: All results are from a three-electrode half-cell in acid. No membrane electrode assembly or full-cell test yet. Details: https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/thesis-bi-pt-formic-acid/
- Making the catalyst synthesis safe to scale (Aug – Dec 2025, KinCat group, Department of Chemical Engineering, NTNU, Trondheim): Problem: The literature procedure lost most of the catalyst during filtration, and scaling it up made it unsafe. What I did: Ran three batches and changed the route after each one. Key result: An aqueous borohydride step with less reductant removed the ignition risk and gave the highest yield, about 220 mg. Limits: Yield and morphology were the checks here; activity was tested on the thesis series. Details: https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/ntnu-synthesis-scale-up/
- Oxygen reduction on a 13-atom platinum cluster (Jan – May 2025, IIT Madras): Problem: Oxygen reduction limits fuel cell cathodes. How do its intermediates sit on a small Pt cluster? What I did: Optimised O2, OOH*, O*, OH* and H2O on Pt13 and checked each was a true minimum. Key result: Every step of the associative four-electron pathway was downhill in electronic energy. Limits: Electronic energies only, no corrections or transition states, so no rates. Details: https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/dft-orr-pt13/
- Cutting NOx from a biomass boiler (Aug – Nov 2025, NTNU, Trondheim): Problem: An upgraded biomass boiler must stay under 300 mg/Nm³ NOx. Could an SNCR retrofit get it there? What I did: As one of four, estimated baseline NOx, checked the operating window, and modelled combustion and SNCR chemistry in Cantera. Key result: About 60% reduction, bringing NOx to roughly 95–120 mg/Nm³ in the model. Limits: A design study built on incomplete plant data, not a plant trial. Details: https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/sncr-biomass-boiler/

## Skills
- Electrochemical testing: Autolab potentiostat, three-electrode cell, CV, LSV, EIS, chronoamperometry, chronopotentiometry, ECSA, durability testing
- Electrodes and catalysts: Wet-chemical catalyst synthesis, catalyst ink formulation, ionomer loading, drop-cast electrodes on glassy carbon and carbon paper
- Characterisation: SEM-EDX, XRD, BET, XPS, TGA, FTIR, UV-Vis
- Software: OriginPro, Excel, Python (Cantera), Gaussian 16, Avogadro
- Process engineering: Mass and energy balances, technology evaluation, process safety
- Lab safety: Handling acids and reducing agents, inert-gas work, plant HSE and SOP training
